headline: Karissa has had new evening confusion for about two weeks, including leaving the stove on, after a fall on 2026-09-23 and an ED visit on 2026-11-05. The evidence has no results yet for the planned workup.

items.statement: On 2026-11-15 her son Marcus reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, and once she left the stove on. The RN found her oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The plan was urinalysis, medication review, and a PCP visit that week.
items.verifier_note: Every detail in the statement appears in the 2026-11-15 nursing note.

items.statement: She fell at home in the bathroom at night on 2026-09-23, and Marcus found her on the floor. She denied head strike or loss of consciousness, and no injury was noted. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed.
items.verifier_note: The 2026-09-23 nursing note supports the date, location, Marcus finding her, the denials, no injury, high fall risk and the PT referral.

items.statement: PT evaluation on 2026-10-01 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation, and bathroom grab bars. PT will see her twice weekly for strength and balance.
items.verifier_note: The PT evaluation note supports the gait findings, the TUG of 19 seconds, the three recommendations and twice-weekly visits.

items.statement: She went to the partner hospital ED on 2026-11-05 for dehydration and dizziness and was treated and released the same day, with no new medications. At the 2026-11-11 PCP follow-up she was back to baseline per her son, and the plan was close monitoring for two weeks.
items.verifier_note: The ED summary, the encounter record and the PCP note support all the details. These include the ED visit for dehydration and dizziness, release the same day, no new medications, back to baseline per her son, and close monitoring for two weeks.

items.statement: The notes show no urinalysis result, medication review outcome, or PCP visit after the 2026-11-15 nursing plan. The notes also don't show whether the walker, home safety evaluation, and grab bars were completed after the 2026-10-01 PT recommendations.

questions_for_team: Have the urinalysis, medication review, and PCP visit planned on 2026-11-15 been done, and what did they show?
Does the evening confusion need further evaluation, given the 2026-11-05 ED visit for dehydration and dizziness and the 2026-09-23 night-time fall?
Is the stove a safety risk at home, and what supervision or home safety steps are needed?
Have the walker, home safety evaluation, and bathroom grab bars been put in place, and how is PT progressing?
Should the medication review reconcile the active list, which shows both simvastatin 10 mg and 20 mg?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in that window: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, observation stays, and any discharges, with reasons.
Falls check: any falls or near-falls in the window, injuries, and whether fall-risk screening or orthostatic vitals were repeated, given age 85 and beta-blocker use.

Cardiac check: chest pain or angina episodes, nitroglycerin spray use frequency (active Rx since 2020-07-11), dyspnea, palpitations, and any cardiology visits or new cardiac testing for ischemic heart disease.

Medication reconciliation: the simvastatin list has two active entries (10 MG started 2026-08-16 and 20 MG started 2020-07-11). Verify whether this is a dose change, duplicate therapy, or a documentation error, confirm which one the patient actually takes, and flag it to the prescriber and pharmacy for clarification.

Antiplatelet and beta-blocker review: clopidogrel and metoprolol succinate continuity (missed doses, refills, holds), any bleeding or bruising reports, and any new interacting medications added in the window.
Blood pressure and heart rate trend across the window, including resting HR and any readings with dizziness or symptoms, compared with the prior review.
Lipid and metabolic labs: check whether a lipid panel was due or drawn after the 2026-08-16 simvastatin change, and review glucose or HbA1c given prediabetes and obesity (BMI 30+).
Weight trend across the window (weight at last review vs current, percent change) given obesity and breast cancer history, and any appetite or intake concerns.
Oncology follow-up: breast cancer surveillance status (last mammogram, oncology visits, any new symptoms or lumps, any recurrence workup), and whether any surveillance items are due or overdue.

Function, cognition, mood, and caregiver: ADL/IADL changes, cognitive screen results or concerns, mood and social engagement, attendance at PACE center or programs, transportation issues, and caregiver strain or changes in living situation. Also confirm care-plan items due in the window (reassessment, goal review, care plan signature) and document no known allergies as recorded.
